reason: The mechanism half is true (child.kill() SIGKILLs only the PyInstaller bootloader; lib.rs:507-518, shell process/mod.rs:78-81) but the claimed consequence is designed out: every worker runs a stdin-EOF watchdog that os._exit(0)s when the Tauri core's stdin pipe closes (sidecar/main.py:71-87,141; openbb_mcp_subprocess/main.py:29-66; sec_edgar_mcp_subprocess/main.py:16-60), tauri-plugin-shell always gives the child a piped stdin whose writer lives in CommandChild (shell process/mod.rs:67,310-313,363) and child.kill(self) consumes/drops that writer. A live probe confirmed the worker survives a bootloader SIGKILL only while the stdin write end is open and exits once it closes. The PPID-1 pids cited cannot be attributed to an app quit (the R15 isolated stack's own MCP bootloaders sit at PPID 1 by construction).
evidence_checked: Read the exit handler, shell plugin spawn/kill, and all three worker watchdogs; ran an own-process probe against the bundled openbb-mcp binary (spawned on a free port, cleaned up). Live `ps -eo pid,ppid` showed no operator app running, only the isolated stack's MCP pairs.
repro_check: python3 scratchpad/orphan_probe.py: Popen(openbb-mcp binary, stdin=PIPE) -> SIGKILL bootloader 58142 -> worker 58150 alive=True -> close stdin -> worker alive=False after ~6.5s. The worker is reaped by the watchdog, not orphaned.

reason: The two supervisor threads cannot race each other on the environment: both mutate it only through std::env::set_var/remove_var (openbb_mcp.rs:59-60,95-96; sec_edgar_mcp.rs same), and Rust std serialises every setenv/unsetenv behind a process-wide ENV_LOCK write lock (and std getenv behind its read lock) - std/sys/env/unix.rs:50-53,112-123 in the installed 1.95.0 toolchain. The Rust-2024 `unsafe` concern is non-Rust code calling libc getenv without that lock, which is not what the finding claims and is not created by having two supervisors (the proposed fix of moving set_var to the setup thread would not change it).
evidence_checked: Read both supervisors' env mutation sites and the std env implementation shipped with the local toolchain (rustc 1.95.0 docs source).
repro_check: sed -e 's/<[^>]*>//g' .../std/sys/env/unix.rs.html | grep ENV_LOCK -> 'static ENV_LOCK: RwLock', setenv takes ENV_LOCK.write() (line 115), unsetenv takes ENV_LOCK.write() (line 123).
